findings.title: Unauthenticated public intake case-tracker leaks full submitter PII and form payload across all tenants
findings.category: Broken Access Control / Sensitive Data Exposure (A01/A02, CWE-639, CWE-359)
findings.cvss: CVSS ~8.6 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N) — unauthenticated cross-tenant PII + whistleblower disclosure
findings.description: GET /api/v1/intake/track/{referenceCode} is explicitly permitAll in SecurityConfig (line 93) and the controller method carries no @PreAuthorize. The service path findByReferenceCode -> IntakeRecordRepository.findByReferenceCode(referenceCode) is NOT scoped by organisationId, and the controller comment claims 'PII fields are still filtered downstream when the submission was anonymous'. No such filtering exists: IntakeRecordDto.from() copies the entire entity, including submitterName, submitterEmail, submitterPhone, and the raw payload JSON blob. Intake kinds include SPEAKUP, ETHICS_DISCLOSURE, PRIVACY_BREACH, DSR_REQUEST and BREACH_REPORT — the payload and submitter fields therefore contain whistleblower identities, data-subject PII and breach detail. Any anonymous internet caller who obtains/guesses a reference code for ANY tenant receives the full record. Reference codes are 8 random base-32 chars in two segments (XX-YYYY-ZZZZ), but they are shared with submitters over email, appear in logs, and the endpoint has no rate limiting, so they are enumerable/leakable bearer tokens guarding highly sensitive multi-tenant data.
findings.rootCause: The 'reference code is the bearer token' design returns the full internal entity DTO with no field-level redaction and no organisation scoping, on a permitAll endpoint. The DTO mapper has no anonymous/public projection.
findings.evidence: Controller: `@GetMapping("/track/{referenceCode}") public ResponseEntity<IntakeRecordDto> track(@PathVariable String referenceCode){ return service.findByReferenceCode(referenceCode).map(ResponseEntity::ok)...}` (no @PreAuthorize). Repo: `Optional<IntakeRecord> findByReferenceCode(String referenceCode);` (no org param). DTO: `IntakeRecordDto.from(r)` sets `.submitterName(r.getSubmitterName()).submitterEmail(r.getSubmitterEmail()).submitterPhone(r.getSubmitterPhone()).payload(r.getPayload())`.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated disclosure of whistleblower identities, data-subject PII and breach narratives belonging to every tenant. Direct PDPL Article 20/transparency and SAMA/CMA confidential-reporting-channel violations; potential retaliation risk for whistleblowers.
findings.reproduction: 1) Authenticated user (any tenant) submits an intake; capture the returned referenceCode (or read one from an email/log). 2) Without any token: curl https://host/api/v1/intake/track/SU-AB12-CD34 . 3) Response includes submitterName, submitterEmail, submitterPhone and the full payload JSON, regardless of which tenant owns the record and regardless of submitterIsAnonymous.
findings.resolution: Return a minimal public projection (status, kind, acknowledgedAt, slaDueAt, referenceCode only) — never submitter identity or payload. Strip PII unconditionally for the public endpoint, and especially when submitterIsAnonymous is true. Add rate limiting / lockout on the track endpoint. Consider requiring a second factor (e.g. email confirmation) before returning even status.
references: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information
OWASP API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization

findings.title: SCM sub-controllers (clauses, fourth-party, resilience, resilience-tests) use only isAuthenticated() — no SCM module permission (BFLA)
findings.cvss: CVSS ~7.1 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) — any authenticated user can read+write supply-chain resilience data
findings.description: The primary ScmController correctly gates every endpoint with hasPermission('SCM','READ'|'WRITE'|'DELETE'). The four newer SCM sub-controllers (contract clauses, fourth-party exposure, supplier resilience alternates/exit-plans, supplier resilience tests) gate every endpoint with only @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()"). Because authorities follow MODULE_ACTION naming (ModulePermissionEvaluator) and there is no path rule for /api/scm/** in SecurityConfig, ANY authenticated principal — e.g. an AUDITOR or a privacy-only user with zero SCM authorities — can read and mutate supplier exit plans (disengagement playbooks, data-migration & knowledge-transfer plans), contract clause templates, alternate-supplier records, and resilience-test results. Mutating endpoints (create/update/approve/reject/activate/archive/record-test/complete) are equally exposed, so a non-SCM user can approve an exit plan or mark a resilience test passed. This is a function-level authorization gap: the resource is SCM data but the check is merely 'logged in'.
findings.rootCause: Sub-controllers were added without re-using the module-permission convention applied by ScmController; isAuthenticated() was used as a placeholder and never tightened. No defence-in-depth path matcher exists for /api/scm/**.
findings.evidence: SupplierResilienceController: every method annotated `@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")` (e.g. lines 65-69 createAlt, 125-129 approvePlan). FourthPartyExposureController has no @SecurityRequirement and `@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")` on create/update/validate/mitigate/retire. Contrast ScmController line 53 `@PreAuthorize("hasPermission('SCM','WRITE')")`.
findings.impact: Cross-functional users can read sensitive third-party-risk material (exit strategies, fourth-party concentration, contract clause libraries) and tamper with resilience evidence, undermining SAMA outsourcing/operational-resilience controls. Combined with the multi-tenant scoping at the service layer it is not cross-tenant, but it is a broad intra-tenant privilege escalation.
findings.reproduction: 1) Log in as a user holding only e.g. PRIVACY_READ (no SCM_* authority). 2) GET /api/scm/resilience/exit-plans -> 200 with full plans. 3) POST /api/scm/resilience/exit-plans/{id}/approve -> approves a plan the user has no SCM rights to.
findings.resolution: Replace isAuthenticated() with hasPermission('SCM','READ') on GET endpoints and hasPermission('SCM','WRITE') (or DELETE) on mutating endpoints, matching ScmController. Add a belt-and-braces SecurityConfig rule requiring an SCM authority for /api/scm/**.
references: OWASP API5:2023 Broken Function Level Authorization

findings.title: Tenant AML officer can inject/poison platform-global sanctions lists (OFAC/UN/EU) consumed by every tenant
findings.category: Broken Access Control / Improper Authorization (A01, CWE-639)
findings.cvss: CVSS ~6.5 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:H/A:N) — cross-tenant data-integrity poisoning of shared screening lists
findings.description: Platform-global sanctions lists are stored with organisation_id IS NULL and are visible to (and screened by) every tenant via findVisibleTo / findActiveVisibleTo. SanctionsListService.update() deliberately blocks edits to global lists from a tenant context ('Cannot edit platform-global list ... from tenant context'). However bulkImportEntries() and refresh() use the same loadOrThrow()->findByIdVisibleTo() lookup, which returns global lists to any tenant, and neither method applies the same org-NULL guard. A tenant AML_OFFICER (the role required by POST /lists/{id}/entries/bulk-import) can therefore append arbitrary entries to a global OFAC/UN/EU list. Imported rows take row.setOrganisationId(l.getOrganisationId()) = NULL, so they become globally visible. This lets one tenant inject false sanctions entries (causing false-positive hits and operational blocking for all other tenants) — or, if combined with future delete/refresh-overwrite logic, suppress entries.
findings.rootCause: Inconsistent authorization across write paths: the org-NULL global-list guard exists only in update(), not in bulkImportEntries() or refresh(). findByIdVisibleTo intentionally returns shared global lists, so 'visible' is wrongly treated as 'writable'.
findings.evidence: update(): `if (l.getOrganisationId() == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot edit platform-global list ..."); }`. bulkImportEntries(): `SanctionsList l = loadOrThrow(req.listId()); ... row.setOrganisationId(l.getOrganisationId()); entryRepo.save(row);` with NO org-NULL check. loadOrThrow -> `listRepo.findByIdVisibleTo(id, org())` which matches `l.organisationId IS NULL OR l.organisationId = :orgId`.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant integrity compromise of a financial-crime control: a single tenant can degrade sanctions-screening accuracy for all tenants (mass false positives blocking onboarding, or noise masking true hits), violating SAMA AML/CFT obligations.
findings.reproduction: 1) As AML_OFFICER in tenant 2, GET /api/v1/aml/sanctions/lists, note a global list id (organisationId null, e.g. OFAC). 2) POST /api/v1/aml/sanctions/lists/{id}/entries/bulk-import with listId={id} and fabricated entries. 3) The entries persist with organisation_id NULL. 4) As any user in tenant 3, POST /checks against that list — fabricated entries now produce hits.
findings.resolution: Apply the same org-NULL guard in bulkImportEntries() and refresh(): only the platform admin (cross-tenant scope) may write to organisation_id IS NULL lists; tenant officers may write only to lists they own (l.getOrganisationId() != null && equals(org())).
references: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization

findings.title: Mass assignment via raw JPA-entity request bodies on create (FourthPartyExposure, SupplierResilienceTest); persistence-layer org guard not wired in
findings.category: Mass Assignment / Improper Input Handling (A08, CWE-915)
findings.cvss: CVSS ~5.4 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:L) — workflow/state-field tampering and soft-delete via unfiltered create
findings.description: Several endpoints bind the JPA @Entity directly as the @RequestBody and persist it. FourthPartyExposureController.create(@RequestBody FourthPartyExposure req) and SupplierResilienceTestController.create(@RequestBody SupplierResilienceTest req) pass the client-supplied entity to repo.save() after only overriding organisationId and nulling id. The FourthPartyExposure entity exposes writable setters for workflow/state and audit columns — status, concentrationRisk, isDeleted, isActive, lastValidatedBy, validatorName, createdBy, updatedBy, rowVersion. A caller can therefore POST a record pre-set to status=VALIDATED with an arbitrary validatorName (bypassing the validate() workflow step), or set isDeleted=1 / isActive=0 at creation. The validate() invariant check only constrains dependencyType/downstreamCriticality/status enum membership — it does not stop status=VALIDATED or audit-field spoofing. organisationId itself is overridden so cross-tenant create is not possible, and update() copies a field whitelist so update is safe; the exposure is on create. Note also that the documented platform backstop (TenantWriteGuardInterceptor / TenantContext.allowCrossTenantWrite) is explicitly NOT wired in yet (see TenantContext lines 74-81), so there is no persistence-layer net catching entity mass-assignment.
findings.rootCause: Controllers accept and persist mutable persistence entities instead of constrained request DTOs; no @Valid; the create path does repo.save(req) on the attacker-controlled object graph.
findings.evidence: FourthPartyExposureService.create: `validate(req); req.setOrganisationId(TenantContext.getCurrentTenant()); req.setId(null); FourthPartyExposure saved = repo.save(req);`. Entity has `private String status = "DISCOVERED"; private String validatorName; private Short isDeleted = 0;` all with Lombok @Setter. Controller: `public ResponseEntity<FourthPartyExposure> create(@RequestBody FourthPartyExposure req)`.
findings.impact: Integrity tampering of third-party-risk records: fabricated validation status/validator attribution, immediate soft-deletion or deactivation at create, and forged created_by/row_version audit metadata — eroding the auditability the GRC platform exists to provide.
findings.reproduction: 1) POST /api/scm/fourth-party with body {"primaryVendorName":"x","fourthPartyName":"y","dependencyType":"SOFTWARE","downstreamCriticality":"HIGH","serviceDescriptionEn":"z","status":"VALIDATED","validatorName":"CISO","isDeleted":0,"createdBy":999}. 2) The persisted row reflects the attacker-chosen status/validatorName/createdBy.
findings.resolution: Bind a constrained request DTO (only client-settable fields) for create/update and map server-side; never expose status/concentrationRisk/isDeleted/isActive/createdBy/validatorName as inbound fields. Add @Valid. Wire the documented Hibernate TenantWriteGuardInterceptor as defence-in-depth.
references: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures

findings.title: ScmService silently defaults to organisation 1 when TenantContext is empty (fail-open tenant scoping)
findings.cvss: CVSS ~4.2 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N) — fail-open default tenant on missing context
findings.description: ScmService.orgId() returns TenantContext.getCurrentTenant(), and when that is null it falls back to 1L: `Long id = TenantContext.getCurrentTenant(); return id != null ? id : 1L;`. Every other audited financial-crime service (Fraud, Sharia, RRP, OpRes, AML) uses TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(), which throws if the tenant is missing (fail closed). If any code path ever invokes ScmService without an established TenantContext (e.g. a future scheduler, async task, mis-ordered filter, or a test/util path), reads and writes would silently bind to tenant 1's data — reading tenant 1's vendors/contracts or writing new rows into tenant 1. The IntakeService author chose the opposite (throws IllegalStateException on null tenant), confirming the intended platform convention is fail-closed.
findings.rootCause: Defensive 'default to org 1' shortcut instead of failing closed; diverges from the requireOrganisationId() convention used everywhere else.
findings.evidence: `private Long orgId() { Long id = TenantContext.getCurrentTenant(); return id != null ? id : 1L; }` — used by every read/write in ScmService (e.g. listVendors, createVendor, stats).
findings.impact: Under any future context-loss condition, SCM operations would silently operate on tenant 1 instead of erroring, risking cross-tenant read/write of vendor, contract and incident data. Low today because the JWT filter normally sets the tenant on authenticated requests.
findings.reproduction: Static/architectural: invoke any ScmService read with TenantContext cleared (e.g. from a scheduled job or test harness) — it returns tenant 1's data instead of throwing.
findings.resolution: Replace the 1L fallback with TenantContext.requireOrganisationId() so SCM fails closed like the other modules.
references: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

findings.title: Missing @Valid and unbounded page sizes on raw-entity / map request bodies in change_mgmt and SCM sub-controllers
findings.cvss: CVSS ~3.7 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L) — unvalidated input and large-page DoS surface
findings.description: ChangeManagementController binds raw entities (ChangeRequest, ChangeApproval, ChangeTask, ChangeLink, ChangeComment) as @RequestBody with no @Valid; the service applies only ad-hoc null/blank checks. Several list endpoints accept a caller-controlled page size with no upper bound: ContractClauseController list defaults size=200 (line 31) and FourthPartyExposureController/SupplierResilienceController/SupplierResilienceTestController default size=100, all passed straight into PageRequest.of(page, size) with no clamp — a caller may request an arbitrarily large page (e.g. ?size=1000000) and force the DB to materialise an unbounded result set. The change_mgmt entity binding also creates a minor mass-assignment surface for child rows (e.g. ChangeApproval), though the parent organisation scope is enforced via require(changeId) and the children carry no organisationId column, so integrity impact is limited.
findings.rootCause: Controllers omit Bean Validation and rely on entity binding; pagination size parameters are not capped.
findings.evidence: `public ChangeRequest create(@RequestBody ChangeRequest body)` (no @Valid). `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "200") int size ... PageRequest.of(page, size)` in ContractClauseController.list. `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "100") int size` in FourthPartyExposureController.list.
findings.impact: Unvalidated payloads can persist malformed/oversized state-machine data; uncapped page size enables a low-effort resource-exhaustion vector against the database and JSON serializer.
findings.reproduction: 1) GET /api/scm/contract-clauses?size=1000000 -> server attempts to load up to a million rows. 2) POST /api/v1/changes with a body missing required fields -> bypasses Bean Validation, relying solely on DB constraints.
findings.resolution: Introduce validated request DTOs (with @Valid) for change_mgmt write endpoints; clamp page size to a sane maximum (e.g. Math.min(size, 200)) or use @PageableDefault with a configured max-page-size.
references: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
